questions.q: Why isn't "I ran the notebooks successfully once" good enough for this pipeline?
options: The Store Operations lead checks the table every morning, so it needs to be ready every morning without anyone remembering to click run
PySpark notebooks delete themselves after one successful run
Delta tables expire automatically after 24 hours
Bronze, Silver, and Gold tables can only be queried once per day
questions.explain: A daily reporting requirement needs a pipeline that runs itself automatically on a schedule, not one that depends on a person remembering to trigger it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson stay at the concept level (schedule, tasks, dependencies) instead of walking through a specific platform's scheduling UI?
options: Because the orchestration shape is identical on both Azure Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, even though their screens differ
Because neither platform actually supports scheduled jobs
Because scheduling notebooks is not possible outside of a command line
Because this course only teaches Databricks, never Fabric
questions.explain: This course serves both Azure/Fabric Data Engineer and Databricks/Lakehouse Engineer students, so it teaches the portable concept rather than favoring one platform's UI.

questions.q: Why does the clean-silver task need an explicit depends_on: [land-bronze] rule?
options: Without it, a scheduler might run Silver's cleaning step before Bronze has actually finished loading that day's data
Delta tables require all tasks to run in alphabetical order by default
depends_on is only a cosmetic label with no effect on execution order
PySpark cannot read a table that was created earlier the same day
questions.explain: Explicit dependencies guarantee each task only starts after the one before it has actually succeeded, preserving the Bronze-to-Silver-to-Gold order.

questions.q: Why does the chosen trigger time (05:00) matter, according to the lesson?
options: It has to account for when the upstream in-store POS export is actually guaranteed to have landed, or the job will run against incomplete data
05:00 is a fixed requirement of every Delta Lake job scheduler
Trigger time has no real effect as long as the job eventually runs once per day
Running before sunrise reduces Spark cluster costs by half
questions.explain: Scheduling too early, before the source data is ready, would run the whole pipeline against yesterday's incomplete data without anyone noticing right away.

questions.q: Why does this lesson wire an on_failure alert into the job instead of letting a failed run go unnoticed?
options: A silently failing scheduled job is worse than no automation — the stakeholder would keep trusting a Gold table that stopped updating
Alerts are required by Delta Lake's transaction log to allow writes
on_failure alerts automatically fix the underlying bug in the pipeline
Without an alert, Bronze data would be permanently deleted
questions.explain: A failure alert gets a human's attention the same day a run breaks, rather than letting stale data go unnoticed for days or weeks.
